To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the military government of Myanmar (Burma) has used the school system to promote its own version of history, which has been designed to serve the interests of the state, not to provide an accurate account of events.
1) The military regime in Myanmar has been very active in shaping the history curriculum in order to promote a sense of national identity and belonging.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which history textbooks are used in Myanmar to promote national identity.
the ways in which the state has used education to construct a national identity, and with the ways inwhich this identity is received by the public.
the ways in which history curricula have been used to build the Myanmar nation-state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Myanmar’s history curriculum has undergone significant change since independence.
the Myanmar history curriculum was a textbook case of nation building.
the history textbooks in the Myanmar curriculum are a textbook case of nation building.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Myanmar government is attempting to build a nation by using history as the main tool.
the military regime of Burma/Myanmar has been very successful in creating and implementing a national curriculum that has served to unify the country and promote the national interest.
the military has been the most successful at building a sense of national identity among its own members and the least successful at building a national identity among the general population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the military regime has been remarkably successful in its attempts to construct a national history curriculum that serves its political purposes.
history education has served as a key site for the construction of a unified national identity in Myanmar.

the military regimes in Myanmar were able to use history textbooks to construct a narrative of national identity that is both inclusive of the majority Burman population and the ethnic minorities, and that also justifies the role of the military as the ultimate guarantor of the nation’s survival.
